title: sigmoid-backed-autoscaler-with-tenant-burst-floors-and-graceful-shedding
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed sustained small microbursts from several tenants that caused headroom churn and elevated P95 latency due to aggressive binary scale-ups. Existing proportional and step scalers overshoot or react too late. This PR introduces a sigmoid-based autoscaling controller that produces a smooth, saturating score for scaling decisions, combined with a per-tenant burst-floor token pool and a graceful shedding path when capacity is exhausted.

What it does: Implements a sigmoid scoring function that maps recent utilization and request slope into a continuous scale signal (0..1). The signal feeds into a capacity allocator that respects a tenant-specific burst_floor_tokens budget and a global gentle_shed_ratio. When capacity is scarce, the controller first attempts to reallocate soft tokens from low-priority tenants, then gracefully shed (queue with prioritized timeouts and optional 503s) according to configured shed_ratio instead of instantaneous hard throttles.

Key knobs added: burst_floor_tokens (per-tenant, default 200 token-equivalent), sigmoid_sensitivity (controls slope), min_scale_score (floor for scale to prevent flapping), cooldown_ms (per-tenant cooldown), gentle_shed_ratio (percent of requests to shed under severe contention). All knobs are exposed via the existing autoscaler CRD and through the Redwood Console config surface.

Telemetry and observability: emits tenant_sigmoid_score, tenant_burst_budget, tenant_burst_floor, shed_decision{yes/no}, graceful_shed_ratio_active, and allocator_rebalanced events. Dashboards updated in docs/observability/autoscaler-metrics.md. Included Prometheus histograms for decision latency and exporter labels for tenant_id and priority class.

Safety and rollout: Feature is gated by a feature-flag (autoscale.v2.sigmoid) and disabled by default. Rollout plan: enable in staging, run a 24h controlled canary on a subset of low-risk tenants, monitor P50/P95 latency and dropped request rate; then expand to bursty tenants with gradual sensitivity increments and final global rollout. Backout path: revert flag, automatic fallback to legacy proportional scaler.

Tests and validation: unit tests for sigmoid math and thresholding, integration tests that simulate mixed-tenancy bursts and verify that total headroom and P95 latency improve vs. baseline. Benchmarks show a 12% reduction in unnecessary scale-ups for synthetic burst patterns used in benchmark-lab.

Related work: follows proposals in ENG-1892 and ties into the tenant-reservation ledger changes in ENG-2034. Addresses customer reports in SUP-473 about repeated transient scale flaps in Dedicated clusters.

ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (ran in ephemeral staging cluster)
release_notes: Introduce sigmoid-based autoscaler with per-tenant burst floors and graceful shedding. Improves stability for microburst workloads and reduces unnecessary scale-ups. Feature gated; disabled by default. See observability guide for new metrics.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated; staging validation -> 24h canary on low-risk tenants -> expand sensitivity -> global enable. Quick revert by disabling autoscale.v2.sigmoid flag or rolling config to previous autoscaler version.
performance_impact: +5% controller CPU for score computation under worst-case high-tenant churn; net cluster cost reduction observed in benchmarks due to fewer scale events.
notes: This PR focuses on control-plane policy and allocator behavior only. It does not modify model-serving runtime or per-model concurrency limits. Operators should handle knob tuning per-cluster based on traffic profiles.
